rules.covers: API keys, tokens and credentialed URLs written as literals in endpoints and functions; the Twilio token in acme_notify_sms is the case the customer described

ask_parts_not_covered.part: passwords hardcoded in a function or endpoint
secrets in tasks, AI tools, middleware, messages (customer said function or endpoint only)

assumptions: The customer's 'endpoint' is object kind query (API endpoints) and 'function' is object kind function
Tags soc2 and pci-dss are acceptable policy tags; the workspace may not have them, but policy tags are not object tags so no workspace check applies
Default locations (definition, agent_settings) and default patterns (all) are right for this ask
The contractor's Twilio secret is the acme_notify_sms function literal
workspace_names_used: env RESEND_API_KEY, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, SHIPFAST_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, PLAID_CLIENT_ID, PLAID_SECRET
confusions: The skill and template say 'Words: password' for SEC-012, but the literal.credential_shape check has no password pattern; the template's keywords overstate what it matches. The customer's password half is not covered and the template does not say so.

The check's description says the pattern list is for credential shapes, and literal_keys covers literal keys passed to specific statements, not a generic password assignment. It is not clear whether a plain password assignment in a stack is a literal_keys match or nothing.

The brief said to write a policy only where a check can help; SEC-012 fits, but the template's 'Fill: nothing' with no examples meant I had to choose object_kinds myself, and the skill does not say whether to scope a secret rule by object kind or leave it everywhere.

The skill says to name only workspace names; for the literal check there is no name to match, so the scope choice was mine. Guidance on when to scope a secret rule to endpoints/functions versus every object kind would help.

I could not run xano policy evaluate (forbidden in this run), so the predicted finding on acme_notify_sms is unverified. Note the skill is written for a live evaluation step I was not allowed to take.
wished_for: A recipe or template variant for 'no hardcoded passwords', or a documented statement that generic password assignments are out of scope for literal.credential_shape
Guidance on the 'secret rotation' part of a secret-in-code ask: that the rule finds the literal but cannot make the old value dead
An example of object_kinds scoping for literal.credential_shape in the catalogue (the example list only shows locations and patterns)
why_confidence: The check matches the credential shapes the customer's Twilio key is in and the rule parses with no warnings, so the key case should be caught. Confidence is medium, not high, because the ask also names passwords, which the check does not match, and because I could not run evaluate to confirm the finding on acme_notify_sms.
